o1.biggest_strength: It turns the 58% migration-ticket problem into hard gates: three staged waves sized from the 420,000 list, a no-go rule, a support rota and a day-4 hold trigger. It also moves Product Hunt and Hacker News to 15 December so they come after the rollout is safe.
o1.biggest_mistake: The launch-day X post and the email thank the community in general rather than naming specific extension authors, which falls short of the 'always credit the authors' principle.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name three or four specific authors and their extensions in the X post and the email, and test-read the copy against grade 8.

o2.biggest_strength: The gates are strong and practical. It requires 1,000 real-setup beta users with zero losses, cuts any claim for features not in the build, and uses engineers who are idle during the freeze to staff support in launch week.
o2.biggest_mistake: The email goes to all 420,000 users on day one and tells them to 'Check for updates' now. That undoes its own staged rollout, which was the safeguard against a repeat of the migration flood.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Match the email to the staged waves, give each timeline row an owner from the small team, and get creators their builds earlier than 24 November.

reason: Output 1 gives me a plan I could actually run with my tiny team: owners on every row, waves tied to ticket limits, and a plan B. Output 2 has good ideas, but its launch email would undo its own staged rollout.
